title: Garmin Forerunner 165 Music targets runners who want premium GPS without the flagship price
summary: Garmin has released the Forerunner 165 Music, a new GPS running watch designed for everyday runners who desire premium features like a bright AMOLED display, reliable GPS, and on-wrist music at a more accessible price point. This model aims to bridge the gap between entry-level trackers and high-end flagship watches, offering features previously found in pricier models to a broader audience. It serves Garmin's strategy to retain its user base and appeal to serious amateur runners who are not looking for the most expensive devices.

title: TSMC and Amkor sign 10-year deal to expand semiconductor packaging in Arizona
summary: TSMC and Amkor Technology have entered a 10-year agreement to significantly expand advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in Peoria, Arizona, with a $7 billion facility expected to begin production by 2028. This partnership aims to create a more robust domestic chip supply chain in the US by co-locating packaging operations near TSMC's fabrication plant, leveraging technologies like InFO and CoWoS crucial for AI and high-performance computing. The initiative is strongly aligned with the CHIPS and Science Act, aiming to reduce reliance on overseas manufacturing and mitigate geopolitical risks for critical chip production.

title: New BlackBerry tools let governments manage Macs without public cloud
summary: BlackBerry (NYSE:BB) has announced significant enhancements to its Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, addressing the growing demand for sovereign endpoint control, particularly among governments and regulated industries. The new capabilities, expected to roll out in summer 2026, include on-premises macOS management, post-quantum cryptography upgrades aligning with NIST standards for FIPS 140-3 accreditation, expanded multi-tenant support, and secure AI-assisted operations. These updates enable organizations to manage diverse device fleets without reliance on public cloud infrastructure, mitigating data residency and exfiltration risks.

title: UBS AG (AMUB) sells $29.48M autocallable GEARS due June 14, 2029
summary: UBS AG has issued $29.48 million in Trigger Autocallable GEARS linked to a basket of 29 equities, maturing on June 14, 2029. These securities feature an autocall barrier at 100% of the initial basket level with a 22% call return rate. If not automatically called, the maturity payoff depends on basket performance with a 1.75 upside gearing and a downside threshold of 75%, exposing investors to potential principal loss.

title: Old phones, new money: $1.63B in upgrades from trade-ins
summary: Assurant's Q1 2026 Mobile Trade-In and Upgrade Industry Trends Report reveals that consumers received $1.63 billion in value through mobile trade-in programs, a 31% increase from 2025. This growth is driven by rising smartphone prices, the increasing demand for refurbished devices, and the role of protection plans in maintaining device condition for higher trade-in values. The report highlights how trade-ins help offset upgrade costs, expand access to more affordable smartphones, and support a circular mobile economy.

title: Italy's antitrust regulator probes Apple over cloud services under Digital Market rules
summary: Italy's antitrust regulator has launched an investigation into Apple regarding its compliance with the European Digital Markets Act. The probe focuses on whether Apple ensures third-party cloud service providers can inter-operate with its iOS and iPadOS operating systems and have equal access to components as its iCloud service. This marks the first such investigation by the Italian watchdog under the DMA, with findings to be shared with the EU Commission.
